editorial_note: A Victorian natural history museum's specimen catalog. The conceit fuses with the facts rather than painting on top of them: every one of the 63 portfolio companies is accessioned as a specimen with a Latin binomial, habitat, and field-note description; the seven team members are the museum's curators with department titles; the firm's mission, tagline, thesis, and operating economics are the Founding Charter; the open Associate role is a Vacancy in the Department; the history entrance is the Archive Wing reached through the East Door. Contact lives in the Registrar's Office as a real mailto:hello@root.vc. All 63 portfolio companies are surfaced as fully-formed specimen cards in the primary DOM (well above the 90% threshold); a view-source conservator's appendix at the end reiterates the team and collection for the curious.

where_facts_live.firm_name: .museum-name (display title 'The Cabinet of Computational Curiosities') and .proprietor ('Proprietary museum of Root Ventures'); also the .firm-mark in the colophon and the view-source appendix.
where_facts_live.mission: The Founding Charter section (#charter-heading + .charter-body) renders the firm.mission verbatim; the tagline appears as the .charter-tagline ('Seeding bold engineers'); the thesis appears as .charter-thesis.
where_facts_live.portfolio: Sixty-three .specimen articles in Gallery II (#permanent-collection .specimens), each with binomial, common-name link, habitat, and field-note. View-source appendix at the bottom lists all 63 again for completeness.
where_facts_live.team: Seven .curator articles in Gallery I (#curators) with name, title, department, and bio, plus a redundant view-source conservator's appendix.
where_facts_live.contact: Anchor with class .mailto in #inquiries (Registrar's Office card) pointing to mailto:hello@root.vc; backed by careers and annual-meeting links in adjacent cards.

history_view_concept: The Archive Wing — reached 'through the East Door' — sits as a full bordered section of the catalog with a large boxed doorway button labeled 'Enter the Archive Wing' that points to /archive/. Two exhibit cards beneath it preview earlier installations (the CLI terminal and the GeoCities salon) so the entrance reads as a curated way back into the museum's program rather than a generic archive link.
